about:
# Palaver

Quests and conversations with NPCs in a panel beside them, read and answered
from the keyboard, in the look of its sibling addons.

One download for Classic Era and World of Warcraft: Forever.

## Using it

Talk to an NPC: their words, their quests and their options open in a
panel in the look of its siblings, the NPC's face in its corner and the NPC
still in view.

- **Space** (or Enter) answers yes: Accept, Continue, Complete Quest.
- **Escape** says goodbye, with the keys on or off.
- **1 to 9** pick a line, or the reward to take when a quest offers a choice.

A key acts when you let it go, and only on the page you pressed it on: a
held Space never accepts the next quest. On a page longer than the panel,
Space or Enter first scrolls down, so you never accept a quest with its
rewards unseen. In combat, while typing or with a modifier held, the keys stay
the game's. Drag the panel to move it.

A quest's offer shows what the game's own window keeps quiet: its level in
the colour of how hard it is for you, whether it's elite, a dungeon, a raid
or PvP, where it sits in its chain, like part 2 of 7, and the group size the
game suggests.

Books, letters and plaques open in the same panel. Space turns the page,
Backspace turns back.

While you talk or read, the game's interface fades away, so only the panel and
the one you speak to stay on screen. It comes back for a fight, a vendor, a
trainer or a question from the game. Keep it on screen with /palaver hud or
the game's Options.

When a quest offers a choice of rewards, two marks help you pick. A green
arrow sits on the best upgrade for your character, and a gold coin on the
best value, the one that sells for the most. Hover a marked reward to see
why. The arrow weighs the stats your class wants against what you wear, and
Palaver needs no other addon for it. The marks never choose for you.

Every setting is also on Palaver's page in the game's Options, under AddOns.
It offers paper colours too (dark ink on tan paper, applied by a reload: the
page ends with a Reload button). **Options > Key Bindings** lists **Open
Palaver**: one key, or on Forever a controller button, opens and closes the
panel. Nothing is bound until you choose.

```text
/palaver on | off        Palaver's panel, or the game's own windows
/palaver scale 1.1       the panel size: 1.1 is 110%, from 0.7 to 1.5
/palaver font 16         its text, 12 to 22
/palaver keys            the keys on or off
/palaver books           books and letters in Palaver, or the game's window
/palaver hud             the game's interface hidden while you talk, or kept
/palaver camera          the view moves in on whoever speaks, or stays still
/palaver value           the coin on the best value
/palaver upgrades        the arrow on the best upgrade
/palaver reset           back in its place, at its original size and text size
/palaver errors          the last error, if one ever stopped a page
/palaver settings        Palaver's page in the game's Options
```

If DialogueUI, Immersion or Storyline is installed, Palaver stays out of its
way and says so.

## Languages

The NPCs' words, the quests and the game's buttons are the game's own, in
your client's language. Palaver's few words of its own are in English and French.

## Thanks

Palaver's way of talking to NPCs follows DialogueUI, by Peterodox and
Raenore. Quest levels and chains come from QuestieDB (Wowhead for Forever's
newest quests), the quest kinds' names from the game's own tables.

## Building

```bash
bun run check     # everything a commit needs
bun run package   # a test zip in dist/
```

The quest facts come from [wow-data](https://github.com/salty-max/wow-data),
beside this folder.

releases.notes:
Palaver 0.4.0

- New: **Paper colours** show dark ink on tan paper instead of the dark look. The choice is in the settings and applies after a reload. The settings page now ends with a Reload button and a line saying so. Palaver keeps its own panel size and text size.
- New: a key binding. **Options > Key Bindings** lists **Open Palaver** under a heading of its own, so one key, or on Forever a controller button, opens and closes the panel. Nothing is bound until you choose.
- On Forever, the window now tells the Gamepad UI that it is open, so a controller's D-pad can move across its buttons.
- On Forever with the Gamepad UI on, the game can show its blocked-action popup after an options page opens. That is a bug in the game's own Gamepad UI. A reload clears it, and the settings page now says so.

A fix for Forever's launch.

- A conversation no longer risks an error when the game hides an NPC's name, such as a quest giver inside a dungeon.

Palaver 0.3.0

- The interface words were rewritten and fixed in English and French.
- Fix: a label's colon is now removed by whole characters, so accented and non-Latin labels no longer break.
- The interface is in English and French. German and Spanish stay English for now.

- The addon's name in chat now wears the theme's accent, colon included, like its siblings.
- Its reply when there is no settings page uses the family's words.
- The kit's latest fixes, and German, Spanish and French updated.

Palaver 0.3.0

- **The sell-value setting says what it does.** "Best value" read as cheapest in every language. It now reads Best resale in English, Meilleure revente, Höchster Verkaufswert and Mayor precio de venta, in the label, the feedback line and the tooltip.
- **The options page and chat replies are the family's:** the same layout, with every reply a sentence with a capital.
- German capitals after a colon, "Fenstergröße" and "auf den Belohnungen" fixed.
